about: Scenarios for Money slice B (docs/ENGINEERING_SYSTEM.md section 3.2). State is derived from the proof each names. PROTOCOL-class.

scenarios.name: A payment that looks like a bill's end is offered to be judged
given: a bill and a payment of the same amount from the same service, the payment after the bill
when: the review is built from the kept facts
then: one candidate, shown with the bill and the payment, asking whether it was paid
mustNot: a candidate for a payment before the bill, of another amount, or from another service
a candidate that closes anything

proof.check: a bill and the payment that matches it: one candidate, shown with the bill and the payment
it asks in the words that fit: this was paid
a payment before the bill, a different amount, or a different source is not a candidate

scenarios.name: An answer is a label: it opens, closes and changes nothing
given: any answer: Mark paid, Not this or Already paid
then: exactly one event is written, against blinded keys
no loop, commitment or ledger is touched
mustNot: a loop opened or closed by an answer
a second event written
a change on Today

proof.check: the review opens, closes and changes nothing: it names no loop, commitment, ledger writer or journal append outside the one answer
the screen writes exactly one kind of event, in one place
an answer is one event and nothing else is written
it added exactly one event, a judged one, at the end, and altered no earlier line
the person's commitments are exactly as they were: an answer changes nothing on Today
a journal that is not there takes no answer

scenarios.name: Not this hides that pair only
given: two bills far apart, each with a payment
when: the person says Not this to one pair
then: the other pair is still asked about
the refused bill is an open obligation again, not settled
mustNot: both pairs hidden
the obligation settled by a refusal

proof.check: two bills far apart and a payment for each: two candidates
Not this hides that pair only: the other bill is still asked about, and the refused bill is an open obligation again, not settled
a verdict about another obligation does not hide this one

scenarios.name: Mark paid and Already paid are final for what they answered, and the next question in a chain is still asked
given: a candidate or an open obligation
when: the person answers Mark paid or Already paid, in any order of events, or after a restore
then: the answered pair is not listed again
a bill answered Already paid, or with a payment marked paid, is not offered as open
in a chain of reminders the next payment is still asked about
mustNot: an answered question returning
an answer about another obligation hiding this one
one answer hiding a question that was never asked

proof.check: Mark paid hides that pair and settles the bill: neither is listed again, and the other bill is untouched
Already paid settles the obligation: it is not offered again
the answers, folded, are the same whatever order they were given in
paid and already paid settle an obligation; paid and not this each answer a pair; missed is counted only on already paid
in a chain of reminders, marking one payment paid does not hide the question about the next, and the settled chain is not offered as open too
read back from the journal alone, the answered pair is gone and nothing else is
the same answers read twice count once
refusing one payment of an obligation leaves its other payment to be asked about

scenarios.name: An open obligation is asked about for 60 days, not longer
given: a bill with no payment in view
when: it is 60 days old, then 61, then dated in the future
then: 60 is offered; 61 and the future are not
mustNot: a long list of settled old bills answered by habit

proof.check: an obligation 60 days old is offered Already paid
an obligation 61 days old is not
an obligation dated in the future is not offered either
the window is a policy constant, not data

scenarios.name: Already paid measures a missed correlation honestly
given: an open bill and the ledger
then: missed is true only if a movement of that amount and direction sits in the obligation's window and nothing matched it
mustNot: a miss claimed for a movement already matched to another obligation
a miss for another amount, the other way, or outside the 45-day window

proof.check: a movement of that amount in the window from a source nothing matched is a missed correlation
nothing of that amount moved: not missed
a movement of another amount, the other way, or outside the window is not a miss
a movement exactly 45 days after the last reminder is inside the window; the 46th day is not
a movement already matched to another obligation is not a miss for this one
a movement between the reminders of a chain, from a source nothing matched, is inside its window: a missed correlation
the same amount in another currency is not a miss

scenarios.name: An answer holds only blinded keys, enums and counts
given: any answer
then: keys, verdict, what was shown, missed, rule name and version, window
mustNot: an amount, a sender, a day, a word, a key that is a name

proof.check: the judged event holds only blinded keys, enums and counts
no amount, sender, day or word is in it
an open answer carries no payment key at all
a key that is not a blinded key is refused: nothing is recorded by name
a verdict must fit what was shown: paid and not this answer a candidate, already paid answers an open obligation
only an answer of already paid can have missed a payment; an open obligation has no payment; what was shown is named
a rule is named by a short lower-case dotted name, never by free text

scenarios.name: Precision is reported from 20 answers and never decided on
given: answers given
then: below 20: insufficient sample; from 20: a percentage
nothing else reads the number
mustNot: a threshold that switches behaviour on
a division by zero

proof.check: below 20 answers it says so
from 20 it is reported, as a percentage of the answers
and it rounds to a whole percent
no answers at all is an insufficient sample, not a division by zero
the precision is read by the screen and by nothing that decides
nothing else reads the answers or the precision: the review's rules take what was answered as an argument and never look

scenarios.name: Money owed to the person is judged as arrived, with no open list
given: something owed to the person and money in from the same service
then: a candidate in the words 'Looks like this arrived' / 'Mark arrived'
no Already paid for what is owed to the person
mustNot: Already paid on money owed to the person

proof.check: money owed to the person is asked about as having arrived
and nothing owed to the person is offered Already paid

scenarios.name: The review is built the same from the same facts, and only from what was kept
given: kept facts in any order
a quiet service
nothing kept
then: the same items, in the same order
a quiet service's facts left out
'Nothing is kept yet' when there is nothing
mustNot: an order-dependent review
a question about a fact whose key cannot be made

proof.check: the same facts in any order give the same review
candidates come newest payment first, then open obligations newest first
and the open ones, newest bill first: D then C
with nothing kept there is nothing to ask
a fact whose key cannot be made is not listed: a doubt never asks a question the journal cannot hold the answer to
the screen is secure like Recall, reads only the kept facts through the person's marks, and says so when nothing is kept
the review is built from the kept facts, and a quiet service's facts are left out of it

scenarios.name: The review screen is secure, pure in its rules, and reached only from Money moved
given: the review's code and manifest
then: secure window, rules with no storage or clock, a screen that is not exported
mustNot: a screen that can be screenshotted
rules that read the clock or storage

proof.check: the rules are pure: no storage, clock, Android or pattern
it is reached from Money moved, and declared not exported

scenarios.name: A chain of reminders: each payment is its own question, and answers survive reminders added or lost elsewhere
given: a bill restated several times, or a bill that comes every month, with payments
when: the person answers, then reminders are added, sealed later or lost from the kept facts
then: an answered question stays answered; a newer bill after the payment is a new question; the next payment in the chain is still asked
mustNot: an answered question returning
a later month's bill never asked about
one answer hiding questions never asked

proof.check: adversary held: the answered pair is gone
adversary held: a later reminder (day 170) joined to the chain after the answer does not bring the answered pair back; held by 'a later reminder does not change the key'

adversary (was a break, fixed): an EARLIER reminder of the same bill kept after the answer (an older month sealed later, a re-keep) changes the chain's first reminder, so the key changes and the answered pair is asked again
adversary (was a break, fixed): when the first reminder of a chain leaves the kept facts (retention, a quiet service taken back), the pair already answered Not this is asked again
adversary held: six monthly bills of one amount are one open obligation, offered once

adversary (was a break, fixed): after the person says September's rent is already paid, October's bill (30 days later, a new reminder of the same chain) is never offered: the answer settled the chain's first-reminder key for ever, so a question that was never asked is hidden
adversary (was a break, fixed): marking the first month's payment paid hides the two later monthly bills, which have no payment in view, from Already paid (the chain is settled by its first reminder)

adversary held: Not this on each of five pairs of one chain leaves 5,4,3,2,1 questions, then the bill as ONE open obligation ([5, 4, 3, 2, 1]); held by 'one open obligation became two' in ReviewTest at length one
adversary held: then Already paid, answered twice, leaves nothing to ask and counts once (5 not this, 1 already paid, 0 paid); held by set-based counts ('the same answers read twice count once')

adversary held: five reminders at 44-day gaps and one payment: exactly one question, keyed by the reminder it matched (the newest within reach), and the obligation is not also offered as open; held by 'one obligation of two reminders ...' in ReviewTest only at length two

adversary held: a chain of five with a payment for each is five questions, each with its own payment key and its own reminder key, and the namespaces cannot collide; held by 'one obligation, two payments' at length two
adversary held: the obligation and the payment namespaces give different keys for the same id (no key collision between them); held by the 'cand:ob:' and 'cand:pay:' prefixes (no check)
adversary held: answering the same candidate twice is one paid pair and four questions are left; held by set-based counts

adversary held: a chain of five reminders with a payment for each, plus a refused pair, gives the same review in any of 40 orders; held by the sort in Correlator.run and the tie-breaks in ReviewRules.build (ReviewTest shuffles only chains of two)
adversary held: reminders 44 and 45 days apart are one obligation, 46 days apart are two; no review check pins the 45/46 edge of the grouping (held by accident)
adversary held: a payment 45 days after a bill closes it, 46 days after does not; held by accident (ReviewTest pins 45/46 only for the missed correlation)
adversary held: six reminders at 45-day gaps are one obligation; held by accident

scenarios.name: Only a real closure candidate is offered: right currency, right direction, one payment once
given: bills and payments in two currencies, money in and out at one instant, duplicated facts
then: no candidate across currencies; money in is never swallowed as a payment the person made; a payment and a fulfilment of it are one; a payment pairs with one bill
mustNot: a false closure candidate
a lost candidate
the same payment offered twice

proof.check: adversary (was a break, fixed): the same bill and the same payment handed twice are one fact, so one question (build lists 1; the Correlator pairs the one payment with each copy of the bill)
adversary held: the same fact sealed in two bundles (kept under two time zones) loads once and is asked about once; held by the byId map in ObservationStore.load (no review check)
adversary held: a payment cannot match two obligations: it pairs with exactly one bill; held by 'used' in Correlator.run (no check)

adversary held: two bills of one amount from two senders and one payment from the second: one candidate, for the second; the first stays open; held by 'a movement already matched to another obligation is not a miss' only partly
adversary held: a refund restated three times and then arriving: one question, in the words for money that came, and never offered as Already paid; held by 'money owed to the person' in ReviewTest
adversary held: money in does not close a bill the person owes, and out does not close a refund; held by the owner in the group key of Correlator.run
adversary held: a zero amount is no bill and no payment; held by 'o.minor > 0' in Correlator (no check)

adversary (was a break, fixed): 500.00 USD from the same sender is offered as the end of a bill of 500.00 INR (the correlator never looks at the currency, though missed does): a false closure candidate, and one currency equated with another (I-011)

adversary (was a break, fixed): money coming IN at the same moment, amount and sender as a payment the person made is treated as 'the same payment' and swallowed (the paired-move key has no direction), so a refund owed to the person has no candidate

adversary held: a bundle holding both the fulfilment and the movement of one payment is one question, closed by the fulfilment; held by 'paired' in Correlator.run and by LedgerTest's corroboration checks, not by a review check
adversary held: after Not this on that payment the bill is open and its own movement is not called a missed correlation; held by r.closing carrying the paired movement

scenarios.name: The journal's answers are read as strictly as they are written
given: hand-made, restored or merged journal lines
then: only a flat object of the known fields of the known schema, passing the writer's own checks, is an answer; one label per pair; repeats count once
mustNot: an unknown schema believed
a line the writer would refuse believed
a nested object misread as the answer
an answer counted twice

proof.check: adversary (was a break, fixed): an answer of a schema this build does not know (candidate.judged.v2, from a newer build or a restore) is read as version 1 and settles the obligation
adversary (was a break, fixed): a line the writer would refuse (already paid, but shown as a candidate with a payment) is believed on read and settles the obligation: write validates, read does not

adversary (was a break, fixed): an answer that also carries another capability's object with obligation and verdict fields is read from the FIRST match anywhere in the line, so the obligation answered is the other object's ([])
adversary (was a break, fixed): one pair answered both Mark paid and Not this (two devices merged, a restore) counts as two answers in the precision (0 paid + 1 not this for one pair)

adversary held: answers with a number for a key, a list for the verdict, a string for missed, over-long keys, or a paid verdict with no payment are not answers; held by the anchored 16-hex patterns (no check)
adversary held: an answer carrying a two-megabyte extra field is not an answer (it is not one the writer writes), and reading it is fast (37 ms)
adversary held: one answer restored 50,000 times is one answer, and folds in 294 ms; held by 'the same answers read twice count once'

scenarios.name: A question that cannot be answered is never asked
given: a key that cannot be made, a rule name outside the vocabulary, a key that is not a blinded key
then: the item is left out; the others are asked in order
mustNot: a question whose answer the journal would refuse
a tap that throws

proof.check: adversary held: a key that cannot be made for one bill leaves only that bill out; the others are still asked, in order; held by accident (ReviewTest breaks every key at once)
adversary held: a payment whose key cannot be made leaves its bill to be asked about as open, not as a question about a payment the journal cannot name; held by accident

adversary (was a break, fixed): a Keyer that returns something that is not 16 hex characters (the contract is an interface, not a check) puts questions in front of the person whose answer ReviewFacts.record then refuses by THROWING, on the UI thread: a doubt must not ask a question the journal cannot hold

adversary (was a break, fixed): a payment whose rule name (read back from a sealed bundle) is not in the closed vocabulary [a-z.]{0,64} is shown as a question, and tapping Mark paid throws IllegalArgumentException from ReviewFacts.record instead of returning false

adversary (was a break, fixed): the natural next rule name, sms.payment.correlation.v2, has a digit, so every candidate it proposes is unanswerable (the vocabulary refuses it on write, nothing refuses it on show)

scenarios.name: One unmatched movement is a missed correlation for one bill, never two
given: two open bills of one amount and one stray movement
then: one bill carries the miss
mustNot: one payment counted as a miss twice

proof.check: adversary (was a break, fixed): one stray payment of 500.00 is reported as a missed correlation for BOTH of two open bills of 500.00 (1 misses from one movement), so the recall measure can count one payment twice

scenarios.name: Dates, limits and size: the edges of the window, a long's limits, and ten thousand facts
given: bills at the 60/61-day edge in UTC, amounts at the limits of a long, 10,000 facts
then: exact edges, no exception, under a few seconds on the UI path
mustNot: an exception
a window that moves with the time zone
a stalled screen

proof.check: adversary held: the 60-day window is by UTC calendar day: a bill of day 140 is open until the last millisecond of day 200 and gone at the first of day 201; held by '60 days old / 61 days old' at noon only
adversary held: a bill at 23:59:59.999 UTC of day 140 is 60 days old on day 200 and 61 on day 201

adversary held: matching is by UTC day: a payment 44 days and 1 ms after a bill is 'within 45 days', one 45 days and 1 ms after is not (stated in 17a); held by 'a movement exactly 45 days' in ReviewTest, for missed only
adversary held: an amount of Long.MAX_VALUE minor units is asked about and printed exactly; held by accident (long arithmetic is only comparison and division)
adversary held: facts dated at Long.MAX_VALUE, Long.MIN_VALUE, the epoch and a day before it do not throw in the review or in its line; held by Math.floorDiv (no check)
adversary held: a bill with no currency is still listed and printable, and answerable; held by Observation.Builder (null becomes empty)
adversary held: 10,000 facts (5,000 bills in the last 60 days, a third paid) build in under 3 s with a cheap Keyer (408 ms, 5000 items); held by accident

adversary held: the same with the install's real Keyer (a file read and a keyed hash for each key, on the UI thread) is still under 5 s, the ANR limit (295 ms); held by accident, and it grows linearly with the items
adversary held: one sender restating one bill daily for 4,000 days, each paid, builds in under 3 s (464 ms); the pairing is quadratic in the chain; held by accident

scenarios.name: What decides never reads the answers; the screen compiles against the facts it reads
given: the source of the review, the correlator and the screen
then: no file outside ReviewFacts and ReviewActivity reads the counts; the rules read only the hiding sets; the correlator never sees an answer; the screen reads Judged by its methods
mustNot: a decider that reads the precision
a screen that does not compile against the facts it uses

proof.check: adversary (was a break, fixed): ReviewActivity does not compile: it reads judged.[] as fields, but ReviewFacts.Judged has them as methods paid(), notThis(), alreadyPaid(), missed() (the suite never compiles the Activity, so every check is green)

adversary held: no file outside ReviewFacts and ReviewActivity reads the answer counts (paid(), notThis(), alreadyPaid(), missed()); ReviewTest guards fold( and precisionLine( only, so the counters are held by accident
adversary held: the rules read the answers only as sets that hide a question (settled, paidPairs, refused), never the counts and never the precision
adversary held: the correlator never sees an answer: it names no ReviewFacts, Judged or journal; held by accident
adversary held: with 5 answers the precision is not reported (insufficient sample) and the answers change no question beyond their own pair; held by 'below 20 answers it says so'
adversary held: 19 answers say insufficient sample and 20 report, whatever the split; held by 'below 20 answers it says so'
adversary held: at the limits of a long the precision line does not throw
adversary held: no answers is not a division by zero for the missed line either
